checks.a_analysis: I scanned the JSON output and compared it with the source PDF to identify any repeated text blocks. While certain headers (e.g., 'MECKLENBURG PARTNERSHIP FOR CHILDREN') appear on both the cover page and the title page in the source, the output correctly represents these as distinct sections without unintended duplication within the converted flow. The independent auditor's report sections are also correctly segmented to reflect their multi-page presence in the original document.

The heading hierarchy is generally well-preserved. Major exhibits and schedules are assigned H3, while internal notes are appropriately nested under H4 headings. There are no instances where heading levels skip incorrectly (e.g., from H1 to H3). Minor level adjustments for accessibility are within the acceptable range.

I found significant structural issues in two primary tables. In Exhibit B (Page 8), the header row (rows[0]) contains only 8 cells, while the subsequent data rows (e.g., rows[3]) contain 9 cells. This mismatch indicates the label column header was dropped or the grid alignment failed. Furthermore, the 'Smart Start Fund' label in rows[1] has a colspan of 8, which is inconsistent with the 9-column data structure below it. Additionally, Schedule 1 (Page 16) is split into two separate 'table' elements in the JSON (sections[7].elements[1] and elements[2]) despite being a single continuous table in the source document.
checks.b_evidence_source: The table on page 8 (Exhibit B) has 9 columns (Label + 8 data columns). The table on page 16 (Schedule 1) is a single contiguous table.
checks.b_evidence_output: The table in section 'Exhibit B' has a header row with 8 cells and data rows with 9 cells. In 'Schedule 1', the table is divided into two separate elements (index 1 and 2).

checks.a_analysis: The logical flow of the document is maintained. Text blocks, tables, and sections appear in the same relative sequence as they do in the source PDF. Linearization of multi-column notes (e.g., Note 1 on page 9) is handled correctly for accessibility purposes.

Lists in the 'Notes to Financial Statements' section are correctly identified as ordered lists. Although the marker type (alphabetic in source vs generic ordered in JSON) varies, the hierarchical relationship and semantic meaning of the list items are preserved.
URLs such as 'http://www.ncauditor.net' appearing in the footer or text blocks have been correctly converted into functional hyperlinks. No fabricated or broken links were detected during the audit.

checks.a_analysis: The HTML output faithfully represents the visual organization of the source PDF. The title pages, transmittal letter, table of contents, and various financial exhibits and schedules are all present in the same sequence and relative position as the original. Elements like centered text on cover pages and the general flow of the audit report are preserved. Responsive layout changes, such as the conversion of the Table of Contents into a functional list of links, are expected and do not detract from the visual fidelity.

The complex financial tables (Exhibits A and B, and Schedules 1 through 5) are rendered correctly in the HTML. The multi-column layouts, particularly in Exhibit B (Statement of Functional Expenditures) and Schedule 1 (Schedule of Contract and Grant Expenditures), maintain their structural integrity. Headers are visually distinct, and the numerical data is aligned correctly within its respective rows and columns. A sighted user can easily read and understand the table data as presented in the HTML screenshots.

All meaningful visual elements from the source PDF are present in the HTML output. This includes the State Seal of North Carolina and the Auditor's signature on the transmittal letter (PDF page 3), the Clifton Gunderson LLP logo on the Independent Auditor's Report (PDF page 5), and the HLB International logo (PDF page 22). No broken image placeholders or missing content icons were observed.

A thorough visual inspection of the rendered HTML screenshots confirms that no content blocks, tables, or sections have been duplicated. Each part of the document appears exactly once, matching the source PDF structure.
